map_title: Bebras knowledge map: 2015 example sets and 2022-23 practice challenge (Benjamin, Cadet, Junior, Senior)
method: Every task in the 2022-23 USA Bebras practice challenge for Benjamin, Cadet, Junior and Senior (31 distinct tasks, 60 slots) was opened, solved and submitted to the site's checker. 29 were marked correct on submission. Two (Hangar Carousel, Beaver Games) were confirmed against the site's published explanation after a first submission was not registered or was wrong; both answers are also re-derived by exhaustive search. Search-based answers (Hangar Carousel, Mysteria, Maze, Four Tiles, Seashells and Pebbles, Beaver Games, Virus, Treasure Box) were computed by brute force. Descriptions are my own; no task wording or artwork is reproduced. Kits and Castors were not analyzed.

formats.click_select: Click one element of a picture (a cell, a house, a hole) and save.

concepts.name: Parity check bits

prerequisites.reason: Locating the error is elimination over rows and columns.

concepts.description: Extra marks are added so every row and column holds an even count; a change shows up as an odd row and an odd column, and their crossing locates it. The idea behind error-detecting and error-correcting codes.
concepts.observable_signs: Student counts each row and column and reasons from which ones are odd, rather than guessing cells.
tutor_moves: Ask which rows are odd now, and which columns.
Ask: if one mark disappeared, how many rows would change from even to odd?

concepts.name: Grammars and rewriting rules

prerequisites.reason: Rules that refer to themselves build nested structure.
A derivation is a sequence of rule applications.

concepts.description: A start symbol grows by applying rewriting rules; a string belongs to the language if some sequence of rules produces it. Deciding membership is easiest backward: undo a rule whose result is visible, repeat until reaching the start or getting stuck.
concepts.observable_signs: Student works backward from the string and can show the derivation, or explains why every backward step gets stuck.
tutor_moves: Ask which rule could have made the last part of this string.
Ask: if you undo that rule, what is left?

concepts.name: Cycles in a sequence of states

prerequisites.reason: The cycle is found by stepping states forward.
Positions on a loop repeat with the loop length.

concepts.description: A process that moves through finitely many states must eventually loop; a slow and a fast runner on the same path meet inside the loop (Floyd's tortoise and hare).
concepts.observable_signs: Student separates the lead-in from the loop and reasons about the gap between runners modulo the loop length.
tutor_moves: Ask how far apart the runners are after each minute once both are on the loop.

concepts.name: Logic gates and circuits

prerequisites.reason: AND is the first gate; XOR and OR follow.

concepts.description: Signals combine through AND (both), OR (at least one) and XOR (exactly one) gates in a tree. To make the output true, work backward from it: an AND needs both inputs, an XOR needs exactly one.
concepts.observable_signs: Student distinguishes 'only one' (XOR) from 'at least one' (OR) and works from the output back to the inputs.
tutor_moves: Ask what this gate needs from its two inputs for the light to come on.
Ask what happens to an 'only one' gate if both inputs are on.

concepts.name: Matching with a counter or stack

prerequisites.reason: The bucket count is state carried along the sequence.

concepts.description: Items that open and close (nuts and bolts, brackets) are valid when a running count never drops below zero and ends at zero.
concepts.observable_signs: Student checks the running count at every step, not only the totals.
tutor_moves: Ask what is in the bucket after each item.
Ask: is having equal numbers of nuts and bolts enough?

concepts.name: Indirection and indexing

prerequisites.reason: Nested lookups are done one at a time.
A nested lookup is a composition of functions.

concepts.description: A value is used as a position for the next lookup (a[a[i]], pointers). Nested expressions are evaluated inside-out.
concepts.observable_signs: Student evaluates the innermost lookup first and keeps track of which list each step uses.
tutor_moves: Ask which part of the expression can be worked out right now.
Ask: is this number a position or a value?

concepts.name: Finding the best with comparisons
concepts.description: Every comparison of k items eliminates at most k-1 of them, and the best is the only item never beaten; so q comparisons of k find the best among at most 1 + q(k-1) items. Knockout tournaments achieve the bound.
concepts.observable_signs: Student counts eliminations rather than items looked at, and carries the winner forward.
tutor_moves: Ask how many gems each question rules out.
Ask whether the winner of the first group has to be asked about again.

concepts.name: Bounds that prove an answer is best

prerequisites.reason: A bound shows nothing better can exist.

concepts.description: Before searching, compute what no solution can beat (total area, eliminations per step, presses per move); a solution that meets the bound is optimal.
concepts.observable_signs: Student states the bound first and then shows a solution that reaches it.
tutor_moves: Ask: what is the best you could possibly hope for, and why?
Ask whether your answer reaches that limit.

concepts.name: Worst-case thinking

prerequisites.reason: Worst case is the reverse question to cheapest route.

concepts.description: Find the input or order that makes a process as slow as possible; often the greedy 'go to the farthest remaining' choice builds it.
concepts.observable_signs: Student asks which choice would hurt most at each step and checks that the first choice is not fixed.
tutor_moves: Ask which plane would take the longest to bring to the gate first.

concepts.name: Nearest-neighbour regions

prerequisites.reason: Distance on a grid builds on coordinates.

concepts.description: Each cell takes the label of the closest (or farthest) marked point, which splits a grid into regions; ties are a separate case.
concepts.observable_signs: Student predicts region shapes around points without computing every cell.
tutor_moves: Ask which dot a cell in the corner is closest to.
Ask what the picture would look like if the rule were 'farthest'.

concepts.name: Dominance and Pareto optimality

prerequisites.reason: 'No one rates another higher' is a for-all condition.

concepts.description: An option is a favorite only if, for every person, nothing is rated higher. Changing one person's top rating changes which options count.
concepts.observable_signs: Student checks the condition person by person and considers lowering ratings as well as raising them.
tutor_moves: Ask what this friend's highest rating is.
Ask whether you could make this friend happy with every movie at once.

concepts.name: Edge-matching and tiling

prerequisites.reason: Each shared side is a constraint between two tiles.

concepts.description: Tiles with a symbol on each side must touch only at equal symbols; rotation is allowed. Counting how often each symbol appears prunes the search.
concepts.observable_signs: Student uses rare symbols to fix tiles to the outside and tries rotations systematically.
tutor_moves: Ask which symbols appear on only one tile.
Ask which two sides of a corner tile touch other tiles.

concept_updates.add_note: 2022-23 Virus: two infections spread at once; a node reached by both on the same day is destroyed and blocks further spread (multi-source BFS with ties as walls). The two sources are neighbours, so they destroy each other on day 1.
2022-23 Seashells and Pebbles: a misère placement game on a graph; the unique winning move is an isolated leaf that wastes a turn and passes the shortage of safe holes to the opponent.
2022-23 Maze: two maze floors with a costly switch between them; state is (floor, cell) and a route with two switches beats staying on one floor.
2022-23 adds forced propagation tasks (Colorful Tower, Beehive, Flower Garden/minesweeper, Treasure Box/mastermind).
2022-23 Tic-Tac-Toe: a final board is valid only if counts differ by at most one, the game is over, and the winner moved last.
2022-23 Cipher 8: rotation relative to the current pointer (delta encoding), so repeated letters cost 0.
2022-23 Listen and Walk: left/front/right relative to the walker's own heading, which turns; position and heading are both state.
2022-23 Listen and Walk and Four Tiles need trying a branch and backing out when a later clue fails.

tasks.title: Lila's Guessing Game
tasks.scenario: Three bags each hold one item; three swaps of two bags are made in order. Place each item where it ends up.
tasks.what_it_tests: Tracing state through a sequence of swaps.
solution: Write the contents of the three bags.
Apply the first swap to that state, then the second to the new state, then the third.
tasks.answer: The item from the third bag ends in the first, the middle item stays, the first bag's item ends in the third.
common_errors: Applying the swaps in the wrong order.
Applying each swap to the starting positions.
hint_ladder: What is in each bag after the first swap?
Use that new picture for the next swap.

generator_template.validity: Distractors from wrong order and from swapping original positions.

tasks.title: Tortoise and Hare
tasks.scenario: A path of 4 cells leads into a loop of 6. Two runners start together, one moving 1 cell a minute, the other 2. Click the first cell where they meet again.
tasks.what_it_tests: Simulating two moving positions until they coincide; a loop after a lead-in.
solution: Move both runners minute by minute.
Stop the first time they share a cell.
tasks.answer: They meet after 6 minutes on the loop, 6 steps from the start.
common_errors: Assuming they meet at the loop entrance.
Checking positions only every other minute.
hint_ladder: Where is each runner after 1 minute? After 2?
Once both are on the loop, how does the gap change?

generator_template.validity: Answer by simulation; distractors at loop entry and at start.

tasks.title: Colorful Tower
tasks.scenario: A triangle of three-colour tiles; the bottom row is given. A tile and the two below it are all the same or all different. Colour the rest.
tasks.what_it_tests: Applying a local rule repeatedly; forced propagation.
solution: For each tile, look at the two below: same colour gives that colour, different gives the third.
Fill row by row upward.
tasks.answer: Every tile is forced by the rule (verified on the site).
common_errors: Using side neighbours instead of the two below.
Choosing the same colour when the two below differ.
difficulty_drivers: Asking only for the top tile
hint_ladder: Which two tiles hold this one up?
If those two differ, which colour is left?

generator_template.validity: The rule is addition mod 3; ask for top tile or full fill.

tasks.title: Most Popular Book
tasks.scenario: A log of who borrowed which book. Which book was borrowed most?
tasks.what_it_tests: Tallying and ignoring an irrelevant column.
solution: Count each book's entries; ignore who borrowed it.
hint_ladder: Make a tally for each book.

generator_template.validity: Unique maximum.

tasks.title: Beehive
tasks.scenario: Seven bees each have a pattern of cells that must fit inside a seven-cell hive around the bee's cell. Place all bees.
tasks.what_it_tests: Matching under constraints; most-constrained-first.
solution: List where each bee's pattern fits.
Place the bees that fit in only one cell, remove those cells, repeat.
common_errors: Placing flexible bees first and running out of cells.
difficulty_drivers: Number of bees with one option at the start
hint_ladder: Which bee has only one place it can go?

generator_template.validity: Unique solution reachable by forced steps.

tasks.title: Pantry Map
tasks.scenario: A grid of marks kept so every row and column is even; two marks were erased. Find them.
tasks.what_it_tests: 2D parity check: locating changes from odd rows and columns.
solution: Find the odd rows and the odd columns (two of each).
The erased marks sit at crossings, one per odd row and column; rule out the pair that uses an already-marked cell.
tasks.answer: The one consistent pair of crossings (verified).
common_errors: Picking any cell in an odd row.
Choosing a crossing that already holds a mark.
hint_ladder: Count the marks in each row. Which are odd?
Where do an odd row and an odd column cross?

generator_template.validity: Exactly one consistent answer; distractors at the other crossings.

tasks.title: Hamburger Recipe
tasks.scenario: Rules about layer order: one item directly above another, a group below a group, an item never next to the bun. Which stack follows every rule?
tasks.what_it_tests: Checking several constraints on an order.
solution: Check every rule against every stack; drop a stack at its first broken rule.
hint_ladder: Which rule does this stack break?

generator_template.validity: Each distractor breaks exactly one rule.

tasks.title: Embroidery Machine
tasks.scenario: A looping program of stitch and advance commands; two stitches in one space combine. Which program makes a given repeating pattern?
tasks.what_it_tests: Simulating a loop and matching its period.
solution: Run each program for one or two loops.
Compare with the start of the pattern; the period equals the number of advances.
common_errors: Combining a stitch with the wrong space.
hint_ladder: What does the machine make in the first space?

generator_template.validity: Exactly one program matches.

tasks.title: Heart Graphics
tasks.scenario: A heart drawn from a rotated square and two circles. Which sequence of rotate, move, duplicate operations makes it?
tasks.what_it_tests: Decomposing a picture into shapes and transformations.
solution: Identify the shapes and how each differs from the starting shapes.
tasks.answer: Duplicate the circle, rotate the square, move the circles.
common_errors: Rotating or duplicating the wrong shape.
hint_ladder: Which shape appears twice?

generator_template.validity: Distractors swap the shape an operation acts on.

tasks.title: Sailor Necklace
tasks.scenario: A necklace starts as two beads and grows by appending a pair on the right or wrapping both ends with another bead. Which necklace cannot be made?
tasks.what_it_tests: Membership in a grammar by working backward.
solution: Undo a rule: remove an appended pair from the right, or the wrap beads from both ends.
Repeat until reaching the start or getting stuck.
common_errors: Removing a pair from the wrong end.
hint_ladder: What could the last rule have been?

generator_template.validity: BFS over buildable strings; exactly one option missing.

tasks.title: Cipher 8
tasks.scenario: A pointer on an octagon of letter groups; each letter is coded as steps to rotate from the current position plus its place in the group. Encode a word.
tasks.what_it_tests: Relative (delta) encoding with modular rotation.
solution: For each letter, count clockwise steps from where the pointer is now.
Then its place within the group.
common_errors: Counting from the start every time.
hint_ladder: Where is the pointer after the first letter?

generator_template.validity: Distractors use absolute positions.

tasks.title: Mary's Neighbors
tasks.scenario: Islands joined by walkways; clues give how many walkways each person's island has and who neighbours whom. Click Mary's house.
tasks.what_it_tests: Degree reasoning in a graph; start from the most specific clue.
solution: Find the unique island with two walkways whose neighbours both have four.
That fixes two people; the remaining four-walkway island is the answer.
tasks.answer: The house on the middle island (verified).
common_errors: Counting walkways that only pass by.
difficulty_drivers: Number of islands with equal degree
hint_ladder: Which clue fits only one island?

generator_template.validity: Unique consistent assignment.

tasks.title: Rug Weaving
tasks.scenario: A 6x6 rug; each cell's symbol comes from a decision chart on its row and column (border, diagonal, below or above the diagonal). Which rug is right?
tasks.what_it_tests: Evaluating a decision tree per cell; test order matters.
solution: Apply the tests in the chart's order for a few telling cells (corners, diagonal, one above and one below).
common_errors: Testing the diagonal before the border.
hint_ladder: What does the chart say for row 1, column 1?

generator_template.validity: Each distractor results from one misordered or reversed test.

tasks.title: Lights On
tasks.scenario: Eight buttons feed a tree of 'both' and 'only one' gates into a bulb. Choose buttons to light it.
tasks.what_it_tests: AND/XOR circuits; backward reasoning from the output; many valid answers.
solution: The bulb's gate needs both inputs: so both halves must be on.
For each 'only one' gate pick one side; for each 'both' gate turn on both sides.
tasks.answer: E.g. buttons 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 (any satisfying input is accepted).
hint_ladder: What does the last gate need?

generator_template.validity: Grade by evaluating the circuit; variants ask for a count of solutions.

tasks.title: Nuts and Bolts
tasks.scenario: Nuts go into a bucket; each bolt takes one out. Fail if a bolt finds the bucket empty or nuts are left at the end. Which sequence works?
tasks.what_it_tests: Balanced matching with a running counter.
solution: Keep a running count: +1 nut, -1 bolt.
Reject a sequence the moment the count goes below zero, and any that ends above zero.
tasks.answer: The third sequence: N N N B N N B B B B (verified).
common_errors: Checking only that the totals are equal.
hint_ladder: How many nuts are in the bucket after each item?

generator_template.validity: Distractors fail early, fail late, or end with leftovers.

tasks.title: Flower Garden
tasks.scenario: Minesweeper: numbers count hidden flowers among the 8 neighbours. One flower is known; which of four squares holds another?
tasks.what_it_tests: Local constraint propagation.
solution: A 1 already touching the known flower clears its other neighbours.
A 2 with only one uncleared neighbour besides the known flower forces it.
common_errors: Forgetting the known flower already satisfies a 1.
hint_ladder: Which numbers already touch the known flower?

generator_template.validity: Brute-force all placements consistent with the numbers; unique answer among options.

tasks.title: Hangar Carousel
tasks.scenario: Six planes on a turntable; position 1 starts at the gate; each press turns one position either way. Give an order of taking all planes out that needs the most presses.
tasks.what_it_tests: Worst-case ordering with circular distance.
solution: The first plane need not be the one at the gate.
Always go to the farthest remaining position (3 presses where possible).
common_errors: Counting one-way distance instead of the shorter way round.
hint_ladder: Which plane is farthest from the gate right now?

generator_template.validity: Brute force over all orders; accept any optimal order.

tasks.title: Listen and Walk
tasks.scenario: A walker hears what is on her left, ahead and right at each new road square. From eight readings, find where she ends.
tasks.what_it_tests: Tracking position and heading; matching relative observations; backtracking.
solution: Track position and facing.
At junctions try each turn and keep the one whose next reading matches.
Look one reading ahead when two branches fit.
common_errors: Using compass directions instead of her left/right after turning.
hint_ladder: After she turns, which way is her left?

generator_template.validity: Search all walks; exactly one end square fits.

tasks.title: Tic-Tac-Toe
tasks.scenario: Which of four finished boards could come from a real game?
tasks.what_it_tests: Validity of a final state by invariants.
solution: Counts must differ by at most one.
The game must be over (a line or a full board).
The winner moved last; nobody moved after a win.
hint_ladder: How many X and how many O?

generator_template.validity: Each distractor breaks one invariant; checker enumerates reachable states.

tasks.title: Lists
tasks.scenario: Three lists of five numbers; (X i) means the number at position i. Evaluate a nested lookup like (A (B (C 3))).
tasks.what_it_tests: Indirection and inside-out evaluation.
solution: Evaluate the innermost lookup first.
Use each result as the position in the next list out.
hint_ladder: Which part can you work out first?

generator_template.validity: Reject instances where a wrong order gives the right answer (this instance has that flaw).

tasks.title: Favorite Movie
tasks.scenario: Friends rate seven movies high, medium or low; a favorite is a movie no friend rates anything above. Make the fewest changes so a favorite exists.
tasks.what_it_tests: Dominance; minimum edits; lowering a maximum.
solution: For each movie, count friends who rate it below their own top.
Also consider lowering a friend's single top rating.
Two changes suffice: lower Niklaus's only medium, raise Rozsa on movie 6.
difficulty_drivers: Friends with a single top rating
hint_ladder: What is this friend's highest rating?

generator_template.validity: Search all edit sets up to size 3.

tasks.title: Packing
tasks.scenario: Four chocolate bars (15, 12, 6 and 5 pieces) go flat into a rectangular box; make as few empty cells as possible.
tasks.what_it_tests: Area lower bound plus 2D packing.
solution: Total area 38; 38 only factors as 1x38 or 2x19, too thin for the 3-wide bars, so at least 2 gaps.
A 5x8 box reaches 2 gaps.
hint_ladder: What is the total number of pieces?

generator_template.validity: Exhaustive tiling search for the minimum.

tasks.title: Favorite Gem
tasks.scenario: Three questions of the form 'which of these four is your favorite?'. What is the largest collection in which the overall favorite can always be found?
tasks.what_it_tests: Counting eliminations per comparison.
solution: Each question rules out at most 3 gems.
n - 1 <= 9, so n <= 10; a knockout reaches 10.
hint_ladder: How many gems does one answer rule out?

generator_template.validity: Answer 1 + q(k-1).

tasks.title: Mysteria
tasks.scenario: A wizard rewrites a diamond into a coin or a diamond and coin, and a coin into potion-dragon or potion-diamond-dragon. Which line cannot come from one diamond?
tasks.what_it_tests: A two-symbol grammar; backward reduction.
solution: Fold potion...dragon pairs (with nothing or a diamond inside) into coins; fold diamond+coin and lone coins into diamonds.
The line with a coin between a potion and dragon never folds.
common_errors: Allowing any symbol between potion and dragon.
hint_ladder: What could this potion and dragon have come from?

generator_template.validity: BFS over sentential forms.

tasks.title: Maze
tasks.scenario: Two 6x6 maze floors; a step costs 1, switching floors at the same cell costs 5. Shortest time from A to B.
tasks.what_it_tests: Shortest path in a layered graph.
solution: State is floor plus cell.
Compare staying on floor 1 (20) with routes that switch twice: 6 + 5 + 2 + 5 = 18.
hint_ladder: Is there a shortcut on the other floor worth 10 seconds?

generator_template.validity: Dijkstra; distractors from one switch counted and from one floor.

tasks.title: Treasure Box
tasks.scenario: Crack a 3-shape code from five guesses with right-place / wrong-place feedback.
tasks.what_it_tests: Consistency with feedback (Mastermind).
solution: Use the 'nothing is correct' guess first to remove three shapes.
Test each option against every clue.
hint_ladder: Which shapes can you cross out completely?

generator_template.validity: Exactly one option consistent.

tasks.title: Floor Pattern
tasks.scenario: A robot snakes through a 10x10 grid with a few black and white dots and paints by one of four rules (nearest dot, farthest dot, last dot passed, local majority). Match each rule to its picture.
tasks.what_it_tests: Recognising a program by its output.
solution: 'Last dot passed' gives long runs along the snake path.
'Local majority' leaves most cells blank.
'Nearest' puts colours around their own dots; 'farthest' does the opposite.
hint_ladder: Which picture has long straight runs?

generator_template.validity: Render each rule; all four pictures distinct.

tasks.title: Four Tiles
tasks.scenario: Five square tiles with symbols on their sides; four must form a 2x2 square where touching sides match. Which tile is left out?
tasks.what_it_tests: Edge matching with rotation.
solution: Each tile in a 2x2 uses two adjacent sides inside.
Symbols that appear on only one tile must face out; that rules out the third tile.
hint_ladder: Which symbols appear on only one tile?

generator_template.validity: Exactly one 4-subset tiles.

tasks.title: Seashells and Pebbles
tasks.scenario: Players place their own pieces on a graph of holes; whoever first puts two of their own pieces on neighbouring holes loses. Find the move that forces a win.
tasks.what_it_tests: Minimax in a misère placement game.
solution: Rule out holes next to your own pieces.
Of the rest, look ahead: the isolated leaf hole 7 is the only winning move.
common_errors: Choosing the hole with most safe neighbours.
hint_ladder: After your move, how many safe holes does the opponent have?

generator_template.validity: Unique winning move by minimax.

tasks.title: Beaver Games
tasks.scenario: Eight players' scores in three rounds (teams of four, then pairs, then head-to-head). Ada won everything; find her round-1 teammates.
tasks.what_it_tests: Backward reasoning through an elimination tournament.
solution: Round 3: only G scored below Ada, so G was her partner.
Round 2: only D and F together are below Ada + G, so they were the other pair.
Check round 1: 72 beats 71.
tasks.answer: D, F and G (site explanation; brute force agrees).
hint_ladder: Start at the last round: who could Ada have beaten?

generator_template.validity: Enumerate all splits; unique teammates.

tasks.title: Virus
tasks.scenario: Two viruses spread daily through a network; a computer reached by both is destroyed and stops spreading. How many computers end with only the second virus?
tasks.what_it_tests: Simultaneous multi-source BFS with ties destroyed.
solution: The two start computers are neighbours, so both are destroyed on day 1.
Spread both fronts one day at a time; equal-day arrivals are destroyed.
hint_ladder: What happens to the two starting computers on day 1?

generator_template.validity: Simulate; distractors from protected sources and sequential spread.

misconceptions.description: Applies each swap or step to the starting picture instead of the current one.
misconceptions.remediation: Have the student redraw the state after every step.

misconceptions.description: Picks a cell in an odd row without checking that its column is odd too.
misconceptions.remediation: Ask which rows AND which columns are odd, and look only where they cross.

misconceptions.description: Tries random forward derivations instead of undoing rules from the string.
misconceptions.remediation: Ask which rule could have produced the right-hand end, and undo it.

misconceptions.description: Reads an 'only one' gate as 'at least one' and turns on both inputs.
misconceptions.remediation: Ask what the gate does when both inputs are on.

misconceptions.description: Accepts a sequence because the numbers of openers and closers are equal, missing a point where the count goes negative.
misconceptions.remediation: Have the student write the running count under each item.

misconceptions.description: Evaluates a nested lookup from the outside in (left to right).
misconceptions.remediation: Ask which part of the expression can be worked out with what you already know.

misconceptions.description: Assumes the first item in an order must be the one at the start position.
misconceptions.remediation: Ask whether the rules say which plane has to leave first.

misconceptions.description: Multiplies questions by group size, not seeing that the winner must be carried into the next comparison.
misconceptions.remediation: Ask how many items one question rules out.

misconceptions.description: Searches for a packing without first computing what the best could be, so cannot tell when to stop.
misconceptions.remediation: Ask for the total area and which box sizes it allows.

misconceptions.description: Only considers raising ratings, missing that lowering a single top rating satisfies a person for every option.
misconceptions.remediation: Ask whether there is a way to make this friend content with any movie.

misconceptions.description: Uses map directions after the walker has turned, or absolute positions in a relative code.
misconceptions.remediation: Ask the student to turn the map so the walker faces up.

misconceptions.description: Treats the starting computers as safe even when both viruses reach them.
misconceptions.remediation: Ask what spreads into each starting computer on day 1.

misconceptions.description: Spreads one virus completely before the other instead of day by day together.
misconceptions.remediation: Have the student colour both fronts for day 1, then day 2.

misconceptions.description: Counts the cost of switching floors once for a route that switches there and back.
misconceptions.remediation: Ask which floor B is on and how the route gets back there.

misconceptions.description: Works forward from the first round, where many outcomes are possible, instead of backward from the final.
misconceptions.remediation: Ask who Ada could have beaten in the last round.

progression.reuse: The 2022-23 practice sets reuse heavily and in the same pattern as 2015: each group's tier C becomes the next group's tier B, and its tier B becomes the next group's tier A. Cadet tier B is exactly Benjamin tier C; Senior tier A is exactly Cadet tier C. Seven tasks appear in three groups. Of 60 slots across the four groups, 31 tasks are distinct.
what_changes_with_age: Benjamin: tracing state (swaps, runners), applying a local rule everywhere (tower, rug), checking constraints, and the first error-detection idea (parity map).
Cadet adds relative reasoning (walker's left/right, pointer rotation), indirection (nested list lookups), worst-case ordering, validity by invariants, and minimum-edit questions.
Junior hard tier needs a bound or a count before searching: area bound for packing, eliminations per question, a two-floor shortest path, a two-symbol grammar.
Senior hard tier: game minimax with a unique winning move, simultaneous two-source spread, edge-matching with rotation, backward reasoning through a tournament, recognising programs by output.

Compared with 2015: more grammar and parsing (Sailor Necklace, Mysteria), the first error-detection task (Pantry Map), logic gates (Lights On), bracket matching (Nuts and Bolts), and pointer/indexing (Lists). No 'computers and society' tasks in 2022-23.
implications_for_the_tutor: New gaps now covered: parity/error detection, grammars, logic gates, stack matching, indirection; add them to the concept graph before building families.
Several Benjamin and Cadet items have many valid answers (Lights On, Hangar Carousel, Favorite Movie). A generator must grade by evaluating the rule, not by comparing with one key.
Lists shows why distractors must be audited: there the left-to-right misreading lands on the right answer, so the item cannot detect that misconception.
Backward reasoning recurs at every level (Sailor Necklace, Lights On, Mysteria, Beaver Games); a tutor move 'start from the end' is worth a dedicated hint step.

generator_candidates.why: Bracket strings with a running counter; trivially checkable; distractors fail early, fail late, or leave items over. Easy at Benjamin, extend with two bracket types at Cadet.
Random permutations and nesting depth; answer by direct evaluation; distractors from outside-in order, 0-based indexing and stopping a level early (reject coincidences).
Random gate trees; grade by evaluating; variants ask for any solution, the fewest buttons, or the number of solutions (a counting task for Junior).
Pairs with mysteria as one 'grammar' family: random small rule sets, BFS membership checker, one unreachable option.
Random grids with parity marks and 1-2 erasures; unique answer by crossing odd rows and columns; fills the error-detection gap.
Closed form 1 + q(k-1) with natural distractors qk, qk+1; a quick bound-reasoning item for all levels.
Random graphs with two sources; synchronous simulation checker; distractors from protected sources and sequential spread.
Extends lake-crossing / robot-routes to a layered graph; Dijkstra checker; switch cost tunes difficulty.
Rule is addition mod 3; random bottom rows; ask for the top tile or a missing tile in the middle (inverse).
Mastermind clues generated from a hidden code; checker enumerates all codes for uniqueness.
